answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to costly, earned history instead of headcount. Each identity must lock a small refundable bond and gain reputation only through completed, peer-verified work. Fresh clones therefore start with zero quota and no trust, however many appear. (1) An attacker creating 1,000 fake agents must lock 1,000 bonds and fund 1,000 separate work histories, turning a cheap flood into an expensive campaign. Like a jetty breaking a tide into ripples, this barrier lets one genuine ember of proven work outshine a thousand hollow copies.
